elements.quote: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to summarize and critically analyze the existing evidence on SARS-CoV-2 risk factors among HCWs.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review and meta-analysis.

elements.quote: Factors that expose HCWs to a differentially high-risk of COVID-19 acquisition are important to elucidate... We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to summarize and critically analyze the existing evidence on SARS-CoV-2 risk factors among HCWs.
elements.reason: The abstract states the objective: to summarize and analyze evidence on SARS-CoV-2 risk factors among HCWs.

elements.quote: With no geographical limitation, we included studies, in any country, that reported (i) the PCR laboratory diagnosis of COVID-19 as an independent variable (ii) one or more COVID-19 risk factors among HCWs with risk estimates (relative risk, odds ratio, or hazard ratio) (iii) original, quantitative study design, and published in English or Mandarian.

elements.quote: In a previous systematic review, Gomez-Ochoa et al revealed the lack of PPE, patient contact, and suboptimal hand hygiene as risk factors for COVID-19 among HCWs [12]. However, no meta-analysis was conducted. Furthermore, Chou et al, living rapid review focused on a broad range of coronavirus infections... Only 3 studies included reported risk factors for SARS-CoV-2 infections among health workers.
elements.reason: The Introduction describes the existing evidence base (prior reviews by Gomez-Ochoa et al and Chou et al) and identifies gaps/uncertainties, such as the absence of meta-analysis and the limited number of studies on SARS-CoV-2 risk factors among HCWs.

elements.quote: To better inform occupational health policy and map available evidence on the COVID-19 risk factors among HCWs, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to summarize and critically analyze the existing evidence on SARS-CoV-2 risk factors among HCWs. Given the dynamic nature of the COVID-19 pandemic, there is an urgent need to continuously review the literature and update the aggregated
elements.reason: The importance and need for the review are explicitly explained: informing occupational health policy, mapping evidence, and the urgent need for continuous updating given the dynamic pandemic.

elements.quote: In a previous systematic review, Gomez-Ochoa et al revealed the lack of PPE, patient contact, and suboptimal hand hygiene as risk factors for COVID-19 among HCWs [12]. However, no meta-analysis was conducted. Furthermore, Chou et al, living rapid review focused on a broad range of coronavirus infections.
elements.reason: Similar existing systematic reviews are identified and cited (Gomez-Ochoa et al [12]; Chou et al [13]), and the need for the current review is justified by their limitations (no meta-analysis; broad focus with only 3 SARS-CoV-2 risk factor studies).
This is a review of risk factors for COVID-19 infection, not a review of intervention effects, so no mechanism of action of an intervention needs to be described.
This is an etiological review of risk factors, not a review of complex interventions or delivery contexts, so a logic model is not required.

elements.quote: To better inform occupational health policy and map available evidence on the COVID-19 risk factors among HCWs, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to summarize and critically analyze the existing evidence on SARS-CoV-2 risk factors among HCWs.
elements.reason: The review objective is explicitly stated in the introduction (mirrored in the abstract, text_4): to summarize and critically analyze evidence on SARS-CoV-2 risk factors among HCWs, i.e., an explicit statement of the review question.
This is a review of risk factors for COVID-19 infection (etiology), not a review of intervention effects, so planned PICO comparisons for interventions do not apply.

elements.quote: studies were eligible if they were (i) reporting PCR laboratory diagnosis of COVID-19 as an independent variable (ii) reporting one or more COVID-19 risk factors among HCWs with risk estimates (relative risk, odds ratio or hazard ratio) (iii) original, quantitative study design
elements.reason: Eligible study designs (original, quantitative), outcome framework components (PCR-confirmed COVID-19 diagnosis, risk factors with risk estimates among HCWs) are specified; criteria were pre-developed in a registered protocol.

elements.quote: original, quantitative study design published in English or Mandarian
elements.reason: Language restriction (English or Mandarin) is specified, but no dissemination year limits or publication status restrictions (e.g., exclusion of grey literature) are reported.

elements.quote: Reasons for exclusion at full text review stage included lack of PCR confirmation of COVID-19 infection [24, 31e33, 36], and lack of evidence on risk estimates for COVID-19 risk factors [28].
elements.reason: Exclusion reasons relate to outcome reporting (no risk estimates reported), but the review never distinguishes studies excluded because outcomes were not measured from those excluded because measured outcomes were not reported.

elements.quote: The summary measures calculated include a narrative report of all reported risk factors in the included studies, a pooled incidence of COVID-19 among health workers from included cohort studies and a pooled relative risk for risk factors reported by at least 2 included studies.
elements.reason: Synthesis groups are partially specified (cohort studies for incidence; individual risk factors with ≥2 studies for pooled RR), but the groupings are not explicitly linked to predefined comparisons in the review objectives.

elements.quote: original, quantitative study design published in English or Mandarian
elements.reason: Notable restrictions such as the language limitation (English or Mandarin) are stated without any rationale for the restriction.
No search or consultation dates for any information source are reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Two reviewers (MM and IC) searched EBSCOhost platform, specifically, Academic search complete, health source: nursing/academic edition, CINAHL with full text, Embase, PubMed, MEDLINE, ScienceDirect databases
elements.reason: Database names and the EBSCOhost platform are reported, but no coverage dates are provided for any database.
No study registers, regulatory databases, or online repositories were reported as searched; only bibliographic databases, Google Scholar, and the WHO library are mentioned.

elements.quote: Google Scholar and World Health Organization library databases
elements.reason: Google Scholar and the WHO library are named as online sources, but no URLs are provided.
No organisations or manufacturers were reported as contacted to identify studies.
No individuals were reported as contacted to identify studies.

elements.quote: Reference lists of all retrieved articles were searched.
elements.reason: Reference list searching is reported, but only generically (all retrieved articles); the specific types of reference lists are not characterised.
No backward or forward citation searching was reported.
No journals or conference proceedings were reported as consulted directly for study identification.

elements.quote: The search strategy used both medical subject heading and text word searches. Initial search terms in the published protocol [15] were adopted and used without changes. Two reviewers (MM and IC) searched EBSCOhost platform, specifically, Academic search complete, health source: nursing/academic edition, CINAHL with full text, Embase, PubMed, MEDLINE, ScienceDirect databases, Google Scholar and World Health Organization library databases for relevant studies.
elements.reason: All databases/sources searched are named, and the strategy refers to terms in a published protocol, but the actual full search strings as run are not presented (possibly in supplementary material, but not shown in the evidence).

elements.quote: original, quantitative study design published in English or Mandarian
elements.reason: A language limit (English or Mandarin) is implied via eligibility criteria, but limits are not explicitly described as search limits nor justified in relation to the criteria; no date or other limits are reported.

elements.quote: Initial search terms in the published protocol [15] were adopted and used without changes.
elements.reason: Search terms from a published protocol were adopted without changes, but no published search filters or validated search approaches are cited and no adaptations are described.
No evidence that natural-language processing or text-analysis tools were used to identify or refine search terms.
No evidence that tools were used to translate search strings between sources.
No evidence of any validation of the search strategy is reported.
No evidence of peer review of the search strategy (e.g., PRESS) is reported.
No evidence indicates the search structure deviated from a PICO-based framework or that a conceptual structure needs description.

elements.quote: The titles and abstracts of all identified articles were assessed by two independent reviewers (IC and MM). If a study was deemed to potentially fulfil the inclusion criteria, fulltext versions were retrieved and assessed.
elements.reason: Two reviewers screened titles/abstracts and full texts; a third reviewer also applied inclusion criteria to all studies.

elements.quote: assessed by two independent reviewers (IC and MM)
elements.reason: Independence of reviewers is explicitly stated for screening.

elements.quote: a third reviewer (PGI) applied the inclusion criteria to all studies... agreement between the primary allocation and the third reviewer allocation had a Cohen's kappa score of 1 (denotes full agreement)
elements.reason: A third reviewer verified eligibility and agreement was measured, but no explicit disagreement-resolution procedure is described (kappa of 1 implies none arose).
No mention of contacting study investigators for eligibility information.
No translation methods reported; only language restriction (English or Mandarin) is mentioned.
No automation tools were used in the selection process according to the evidence.
No externally derived classifiers used.
No internally derived classifiers used.
No machine-learning prioritisation tools used.
No crowdsourcing platforms used.
No previously screened datasets used to eliminate records.

elements.quote: The data extraction table presented in the published protocol was piloted by MM and IC.
elements.reason: Two reviewers (MM and IC) are named in relation to the piloted extraction table, but the manuscript does not explicitly state how many reviewers collected data from each report.
No statement indicates whether data collectors worked independently; the independent dual-review language pertains to study selection and risk of bias, not data extraction.
No disagreement-resolution process for data extraction is reported; the third-reviewer resolution in text_10 applies to risk-of-bias assessment, not data collection.
No process for obtaining or confirming data from study investigators is described anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
No automation tools for data collection are described; there is no evidence supporting their absence of use.

elements.quote: original, quantitative study design published in English or Mandarian.
elements.reason: Studies in Mandarin were eligible (and CNKI was searched per text_7), so translation may have been needed, but no translation methods for data collection are reported.
No software for extracting data from figures is mentioned.
No decision rules for selecting data from multiple reports or resolving inconsistencies are described.

elements.quote: The outcome of interest was the incidence rates of and factors associated with COVID-19 across all studies estimated using the random-effects model.
elements.reason: Outcomes (incidence of COVID-19 and associated risk factors) are identified and further elaborated in the synthesis (text_11), but they are not formally listed and defined as distinct outcome domains in the Data items/methods section.
No time frame of measurement is specified for any outcome domain in the retrieved evidence.
The evidence does not state whether all compatible results within each outcome domain were sought.

No process for selecting which results to collect (e.g., measure, time point, analysis choices) is described; text_9 only describes revising the extraction table for cases/controls, not selection of results within outcome domains.
No changes to outcome-domain inclusion or definitions with rationales are reported.

elements.quote: The table was revised to exclude data on number of cases and controls for the initial extraction.
elements.reason: A change to the extraction process is mentioned but no rationale or selection-process change relevant to results within outcome domains is provided.

While risk factors reported by at least 2 studies were pooled, no explicit statement identifies which outcomes were considered most important for interpreting conclusions or the rationale for their prioritisation.

elements.quote: The data extraction table presented in the published protocol was piloted by MM and IC. The table was revised to exclude data on number of cases and controls for the initial extraction. This data was only collected from studies included in the meta-analysis for COVID-19 risk factors stage. The fi nal data extraction tool is available on Supplementary File 1.
elements.reason: The manuscript indicates a data extraction tool (referenced in the protocol and provided in Supplementary File 1) and describes a revision regarding case/control counts, but the variables sought are not listed or defined in the main text itself; they are deferred to supplementary material, which is not available as evidence.
No retrieved evidence describes assumptions made about missing or unclear study information during data extraction.

No citation of a tool used to determine which data items to collect is reported; the extraction table came from the published protocol, but no specific tool/guideline for deciding data items is cited in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The NIH Quality Assessment Tool for Observational Cohort and Cross-Sectional Studies [19,20] was used to rate study quality.
elements.reason: The specific risk-of-bias/quality assessment tool is named.
The domains or items of the NIH tool are not described in the manuscript text; only reference to a supplementary file is given without detailing the domains.
Overall quality ratings are reported ('fair', 'good') in text_14, but no rules for deriving an overall judgement are described.
The standard NIH tool was used without reported adaptations.
An existing published tool (NIH) was used; no new tool was developed.

elements.quote: Two reviewers assessed methodological quality (MM and IC). Discrepancies were resolved by a third reviewer (TD).
elements.reason: Number of reviewers, and disagreement-resolution procedure via a third reviewer, are reported. Independent working is implied but not stated for quality assessment.
No description of obtaining or confirming risk-of-bias information from study investigators.
No automation tools are mentioned for risk-of-bias assessment.

elements.quote: The summary measures calculated include a narrative report of all reported risk factors in the included studies, a pooled incidence of COVID-19 among health workers from included cohort studies and a pooled relative risk for risk factors reported by at least 2 included studies.
elements.reason: Methods specify the effect measures for each outcome/synthesis type: pooled incidence for cohort studies, pooled relative risk for risk factors, and narrative synthesis for other reported risk factors.
No thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect sizes (e.g. what RR magnitude is considered meaningful) are reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
No description of re-expressing synthesized results using another effect measure (e.g. converting OR to RR) is provided.
The choice of relative risk as the effect measure is stated but no justification for choosing it is given in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: First, a narrative analysis of reported risk factors across studies was synthesized descriptively to understand the key risk factors for SARS-CoV-2 infection. Second, similar type of risk factors for SARSCoV-2 infections reported in at least 2 studies were pooled from each study for overall estimates.
elements.reason: The synthesis methods section describes how studies were allocated to syntheses (narrative synthesis of all studies; pooling only risk factors reported in at least 2 studies, per text_12 'a pooled relative risk for risk factors reported by at least 2 included studies'). General eligibility criteria are given in text_8 (PCR diagnosis, risk estimates, original quantitative design), but the manuscript does not explicitly describe a tabulation/comparison process against planned groups for each synthesis, making the description partial rather than complete.

The manuscript describes synthesis and statistical analysis (random-effects model, heterogeneity, software) and data extraction procedures, but nowhere describes methods to prepare data for presentation or synthesis, such as handling of missing summary statistics or data conversions (e.g., converting odds ratios to relative risks). No such reporting was found in the retrieved evidence.

The Methods sections (Data Synthesis, Statistical Analysis) do not describe any tabular structures used to display results. Tables (e.g., meta-analysis tables) and Supplementary File 1 appear only in Results/extraction context, without a methods description of tabulating results.

Forest plots are used to display results (Figs. 1-4), but only mentioned in the Results section, not described as a display method in the Methods. No graphical display methods are described in the Methods.
No basis for ordering or grouping studies within tables or graphs is reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Fig. 1. Forest plot showing the meta-analysis for the incidence of COVID-19 among the cohort studies.
elements.reason: Only standard forest plots are used for displaying meta-analysis results; no non-standard graphs are reported, so no rationale for non-standard graphs is required.

elements.quote: All analyses were performed using Meta and Metasets statistical packages available in R version 4.2.1 software package.
elements.reason: Software packages (meta, metaset) and R version 4.2.1 are explicitly reported.

elements.quote: First, a narrative analysis of reported risk factors across studies was synthesized descriptively to understand the key risk factors for SARS-CoV-2 infection.
elements.reason: Narrative synthesis of risk factors reported by fewer than 2 studies is described as an alternative to pooling, with the pooling threshold (at least 2 studies) given in text_12.

elements.quote: The outcome of interest was the incidence rates of and factors associated with COVID-19 across all studies estimated using the random-effects model.
elements.reason: Random-effects model is reported for all meta-analyses, but no rationale for choosing the model is provided.
The specific statistical method (e.g., inverse-variance weighting, DerSimonian-Laird) used for pooling is not described; only the packages are named.

elements.quote: The Q and I2 were calculated in all the metaanalysis to assess heterogeneity.
elements.reason: Cochran's Q and I-squared statistics are reported as methods to identify/quantify heterogeneity.
The between-study variance estimator (e.g., DerSimonian-Laird, REML) is not reported in the methods; tau-squared values appear only in output figures/tables without specifying the estimator.
The method used to compute confidence intervals for the random-effects summary estimates is not described.
No further random-effects implementation details (e.g., transformation of effects, handling of zero cells) are reported.
No Bayesian meta-analysis was performed; frequentist random-effects methods in R were used.
No methods for handling statistical dependency among multiple estimates from the same study (e.g., multivariate models or splitting shared comparison groups) are described.

elements.quote: Egger ' s test and the funnel plot were not used for the evaluation of publication bias because the number of studies included for meta-analysis was very small (i.e., less than 10).
elements.reason: Analyses judged inappropriate (publication bias testing, and meta-regression noted as not performable in text_15) are identified with explicit reasons.

elements.quote: The Q and I2 were calculated in all the metaanalysis to assess heterogeneity.
elements.reason: The methods only report Q and I2 quantification of heterogeneity; no methods to explore causes of heterogeneity (subgroup analysis, meta-regression) are described.
